Text:
Orders that initiate the actual lift or move (or any significant change in movement) are given in two parts:

1. {{c1::a preparatory command}}

2. {{c1::a command of execution}}
Back Extra:
Ex: "All ready to stop. STOP!" (the preparatory "All ready to stop" gets attention, identifies who should act, and prepares the team; the declarative "STOP!" marks the exact moment of execution).

Cue: commands of execution are delivered in a louder voice.

Text: To avoid confusion with a lift countdown, the leader should always clarify in advance whether "three" is {{c1::part of the preparatory command}} or {{c1::itself the order to execute}}.
Back Extra:
Ex: "We're going to lift on three. One, two, THREE!" versus "I'm going to count to three, and then we're going to lift. One, two, three, LIFT!"

Why: the two patterns execute at different moments (on "THREE!" in the first, only after the count in the second), so an unclarified countdown splits the team's timing.
